name: Feedback gh adapter
purpose: The single place that shells out to gh. Named seam via RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE so every test replaces gh with a fake that records calls.
responsibilities: Provide ghLabelList, ghIssueSearch, ghIssueCreate, ghIssueComment, ghRepoView (viewerPermission, visibility, hasIssuesEnabled), ghAuthStatus
Never read GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN; never spawn gh auth login; never mutate process.env
Return typed results, not raw shell output; errors carry the classified reason (network, 4xx, 5xx, ratelimit, notFound)
internalStructure: src/feedback/gh.js exports the interface; RCF_FEEDBACK_GH_MODULE names an alternative module (import() at test time) that exports the same signatures. This mirrors the verifier launchAgent override in src/verify/engine/launcher.js.

interfaces.name: ghIssueCreate
interfaces.description: Create one issue on a repo with title, body and labels; return { url, number }. [legacy kind: function; mapped to other per DEFINE spec §5.2 closed vocabulary, 0.30.0 PR 8]

interfaces.name: ghIssueSearch
interfaces.description: Search issues on a repo by body query; return matches. [legacy kind: function; mapped to other per DEFINE spec §5.2 closed vocabulary, 0.30.0 PR 8]

interfaces.name: ghIssueComment
interfaces.description: Comment on an issue; return { url }. [legacy kind: function; mapped to other per DEFINE spec §5.2 closed vocabulary, 0.30.0 PR 8]

dependencies.name: gh
dependencies.description: The GitHub CLI; the tool never handles tokens itself.

tradeoffs: gh is a dependency the reporter chooses to install; the cost is a fallback bundle path when gh is missing, which the design considers a feature rather than a bug.
notes: A future MCP-only harness would call the CLI too; a native gh-lib port is not planned for v1.
